extracted.intended_audience: public relations researchers, measurement professionals, communications executives, agencies, and industry stakeholders involved in PR measurement
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and principles for developing, adopting, and evaluating standards for public relations research and measurement (including social media and traditional media measurement). Emphasizes comparability, harmonized definitions/methods, stakeholder involvement, and multi-year standards development.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISO definition of a standard
rubrics_metrics.description: An ISO standard is a documented agreement containing technical specifications or other precise criteria to be used consistently as rules, guidelines, or definitions of characteristics to ensure that materials, products, processes and services are fit for their purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ISO conception of a standard when developing PR research standards: documented, precise criteria used consistently as rules/guidelines/definitions to ensure fitness for purpose. Treat standards as having potential to influence reliability, safety, and efficiency in their domain; consider them applicable to research and measurement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards can take many forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards can take many forms, ranging from operational definitions to guidelines to absolute rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating PR measurement standards, recognize the spectrum from informal guidelines to strict rules; choose the appropriate form depending on whether the area requires flexibility (guidelines/operational definitions) or strict conformity (absolute rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards apply to processes as well as products
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards can apply to processes as well as to nuts and bolts (e.g., ISO 9000 quality management systems; ISO 26000 guidelines on corporate social responsibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include process-level standards for research and measurement practices (methodology, quality management) as well as technical metric definitions. Reference existing process standards (ISO 9000, ISO 26000) as models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards are voluntary agreements among industry partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards are an agreement, voluntary, among industry partners to deliver benefits to suppliers, customers, and partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat standards as industry-led, voluntary accords intended to benefit ecosystems; build coalition buy-in rather than relying solely on top-down regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards are living agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard is a 'living agreement,' in other words they take time to grow, develop, and mature, and they change over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for iterative development, review, and updates. Expect standards development to be multi-year and to evolve as practices and technologies change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for standard metrics and standard measurement practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of standard metrics nor standard measurement practices prevents compiling comparable data across business units, programs, campaigns, and organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize defining standard metrics and consistent measurement practices so teams can aggregate, compare, and learn across campaigns and organizational units; this addresses practical reporting frustrations (e.g., inability to create a complete picture of PR contribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards enable comparison across programs, brands, business units, and organizations and thus facilitate organizational learning and better public relations practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design standards to produce comparable data sets that support benchmarking, trend analysis, and transfer of lessons learned across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization of definitions and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards harmonize definitions and methods, thus allowing research professionals to focus on designing measurement and evaluation programs, research design, and delivering insights to clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create clear, shared operational definitions and methodological norms so practitioners spend less time reconciling vocabulary/approach and more on analysis and insight generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards boost innovation and competition based on insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards will boost innovation and encourage competition based on insights rather than black boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By standardizing definitions and methods, the market can reward firms that provide superior analysis and interpretation rather than opaque proprietary metrics; promote transparency and comparability to shift competition toward insight quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards enhance credibility of research and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Better research data and better insights will enhance the credibility of the research and measurement function, as well as the importance of public relations in building organizational value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize rigorous, standardized measurement to increase the function’s credibility with C-suite stakeholders and to demonstrate PR’s contribution to organizational value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of inaction: externally imposed standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If the profession does not develop and make visible progress on research and measurement standards, standards will be imposed by large client organizations and/or by purchasing departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View standards development as strategic: industry self-regulation prevents externally imposed requirements that may not align with PR practice needs; act proactively to lead standards formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketplace adoption and customer validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The marketplace ultimately drives the adoption of standards. A customer panel will, in essence, provide a final determination that 'this looks like a standard we can use.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage client organizations and create customer panels as part of standards validation; use market acceptance as a key adoption metric when finalizing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards development is a multi-year, collaborative process
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards development is a multi-year process; they take time to grow, develop, and mature, and they change over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set expectations for long timelines, iterative deliverables, coalition-based working groups, and staged rollouts (e.g., initial deliverables followed by broader adoption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority subject areas for PR research standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Working teams published discussion documents and proposed interim standards in areas including traditional media measurement, ethical practices and guidelines, and social media measurement. Other initiatives include measuring the communications life cycle (awareness, understanding, perception, interest, and advocacy), ROI, and program measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When prioritizing standards work, include: traditional media measurement; social media measurement; ethical practices/guidelines; communications life-cycle metrics (awareness → understanding → perception → interest → advocacy); ROI measurement; and program measurement standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder participation and ways to be involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders can track updates, provide regular feedback on discussion documents and proposed interim standards, share updates on standards with clients, and participate in Coalition member events to comment, link and share information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage broad stakeholder engagement: subscribe to updates, review and comment on drafts, communicate standards to clients, and participate in events to influence and accelerate adoption.
